title: Methods
description: Instance methods, self, and special methods
theory:
### Binding behavior to objects

Instance methods take `self` implicitly when accessed through an instance.
**Class methods** (`@classmethod`) receive the class object as `cls`; **static
methods** (`@staticmethod`) are ordinary functions namespaced on the class. Prefer
classmethods for alternate constructors.

### Calling conventions

You can also retrieve functions unbound from the class and pass instances
explicitly—useful in rare metaprogramming scenarios—but idiomatic code sticks to
normal dotted calls.

```python
class Bucket:
    def __init__(self, limit: int) -> None:
        self.limit = limit

    @classmethod
    def tiny(cls) -> "Bucket":
        return cls(3)


b = Bucket.tiny()
assert isinstance(b, Bucket)
```

exercises.title: Define a Method
exercises.description: Define a method on a struct type 'Person' with a 'Name' field that returns a greeting string.
exercises.starter_code:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
hints: Implement greet referencing self.name on the Person class.
exercises.solution:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
    def greet(self): return "Hello, " + self.name

print(Person("Alice").greet())

exercises.title: Pointer Receiver
exercises.description: Define a method with a pointer receiver that modifies the receiver's state. Create a 'SetName' method on Person.
exercises.starter_code:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
hints: set_name mutates the same mutable instance referenced by p.
exercises.solution:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
    def set_name(self, name): self.name = name

p = Person('Bob')
p.set_name('Charlie')
print(p.name)

exercises.title: Value Receiver
exercises.description: Define a method with a value receiver that returns a new value without modifying the original.
exercises.starter_code:
class Counter:
    def __init__(self, value=0): self.value = value
hints: increment returns fresh Counter clones simulating immutable returns.

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define a 'Stringer' interface with a String() method, then satisfy it with a type.
exercises.starter_code:
class Point:
    def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y
exercises.solution:
class Point:
    def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y
    def __str__(self): return f'Point({self.x}, {self.y})'

print(Point(10, 20))

exercises.title: Method Chaining
exercises.description: Define a Builder type with Methods Add(str) Builder and Build() string. Add returns the Builder for chaining. Test by chaining Add("Hello").Add("World").Build().
hints: Builder.add returns self to allow fluent chaining culminating in build().
exercises.solution:
class Builder:
    def __init__(self): self.result = ""
    def add(self, s):
        self.result += s
        return self
    def build(self): return self.result

print(Builder().add("Hello").add("World").build())

exercises.title: Multiple Methods on Same Type
exercises.description: Define a Circle type with Radius float. Add two methods: Area() float and Perimeter() float. Create a circle with radius 5.0, compute both, and print them.
hints: Reuse math.pi for both area and perimeter helpers.
exercises.solution:
import math
class Circle:
    def __init__(self, radius): self.radius = radius
    def area(self): return math.pi * self.radius ** 2
    def perimeter(self): return 2 * math.pi * self.radius

c = Circle(5.0)
print(c.area())
print(c.perimeter())
